sentence: This project studies how long-term inflammation changes stem cells in barrier tissues and makes them more likely to form cancer.
This project studies how skeletal muscle cells fuse, a process that keeps the many nuclei in myofibers supplied.
This project builds computer tools that detect arterial calcifications on dental cone beam computed tomography images and tests whether they predict cardiovascular disease.
This project studies how mitochondrial dysfunction and proteostasis failure are linked through ribosome-associated quality control in neurodegenerative diseases.
This project studies the different basal epithelial cells in the central cornea, limbus and conjunctiva and their roles in wound healing.
This project develops a technology called structural surfaceomics to find tumor-specific surface targets, defined by protein conformation, for immune cells that fight cancer.
This project uses signatures based on multiple genes to identify and study stem-like T cells that drive disease in animal models.
This project tries to find genetic markers that predict which patients treated with nilotinib develop artery disease, using a cell culture model.
This project studies genomic and epigenomic risk factors for lung cancer in Native Hawaiians, who have greater risk and poorer survival.
This project studies how common genetic variants make people more susceptible to immune-mediated diseases.
This project studies the structure and function of membrane proteins that pathogenic microorganisms use to transport molecules and send signals.
This project develops a small molecule that blocks a histone methyltransferase in breast cancer cells that lack the estrogen receptor.
This project studies how the insular cortex combines taste and visceral signals and how its circuits support taste-visceral association learning.
This project carries out cancer prevention and control research to find risk factors, evaluate preventive agents and put behavioral strategies into practice.
This project builds open-source software that uses deep-learning to detect base modifications in DNA and RNA from nanopore sequencing.
This project works to improve a drug that blocks a protein tyrosine phosphatase in immune cells so it can help fight cancer.
This project tries to find out why breast cancers with chromosomal instability resist immune therapy and tests whether blocking chronic inflammation restores sensitivity.
This project studies whether genetic variation in certain genes controls how the genital mucosa responds to bacterial vaginosis.
This project designs a framework to help doctors decide how closely to monitor patients after major surgery and when they can go home.
This project studies how drugs such as ketamine change brain circuits for spatial cognition, using electrophysiology in animals.
